well_result_type_comment: No reservoir found at Jock Scott. A Cretaceous sequence much thicker than prognosed filled the section that had been interpreted as Upper Jurassic.
main_failure_mechanism: No reservoir present at well location, as a result of incorrect stratigraphic prognosis.
geophysical_update_comment: Two possible seismic picks for the BCU were identified at an early stage of the licence evaluation, as a result of the structural setting relative to nearby wells. The shallower pick was chosen as the 'base case' model, allowing for a thick Upper Jurassic package at the well location, with the deeper pick retained as an 'anti-model' (risked on reservoir presence). Drilling results revealed that the upper pick (prognosed BCU) was a reflector within the Lower Cretaceous, and that the BCU was represented by the lower pick (anti-model). This was a failure of prognosis (interpretation) rather than mapping or depth conversion. All formation tops in the well came in within the prognosed depth uncertainty, however beneath the Valhall Formation the seismic reflectors penetrated did not match the stratigraphic prognosis.
valid_dry_hole_comment: Upper Jurassic (Piper Fm equivalent) sands were not present in the well location, hence this was not a valid test of the Piper equivalent play.
remaining_potential: The possibility for Upper Jurassic sands remains to the north east of the well location, however the remaining prospect is considerably smaller than the original Jock Scott prospect, and carries risk on reservoir presence (as no Upper Jurassic sands were encountered in the well), trap (stratigraphic trapping required to the south) and on migration (it is located in a possible migration shadow).

main_failure_mechanism: Trap definition. The pre-drill key risk was lateral seal to the Skene Field - if connected to Skene then the Skene North location would be heavily depleted and likely non-commerical. LWD pressure measurements of the Upper and Lower Beryl formations indicate that the Skene North location is not in pressure communication with Skene (virgin overpressure found). the small column found at Skene North is not consistent with the large as mapped down-thrown fault trap. It is intererpted that the ultimate trap for the Skene North mapped fualt block is further up-dip along the western Horst that flanks Skene Field.

well_result_type_comment: The well found a gross 27.4 mTVT Upper Scapa (K34) sandstone with 99% NTG and an average porosity of 30.6%, at a depth of -2200m tvdss. No hydrocarbon shows were seen while drilling and the sandstone was water-bearing based on subsequent log interpretation. A deeper gross 6 mTVT Lower Scapa (K20) sandstone was also proven, although very poor quality with a NTG of 1% and average porosity of 13.7%. This sand was also water-wet. No hydrocarbon indications were seen during the drilling of the well.

geophysical_update_comment: The well was targeting a wedge of high amplitude reflectors onlapping the Clashnessie High to the east.  Two  low impedance packages were recognised and believed to contain reservoir sands pre-drill.  The result of the well was that both of these low impedance zone were shale-dominated.  However, beneath this, a high impedance zone (Mid Turonian) was conglomeratic and oil-bearing.  An additional dim low impedance zone (Lower Turonian/?Early Cretaceous) at the base of the wedge was found to be better quality oil-bearing sandstone. Seismic rock property work suggests that  fluid response is not likely in this discovery, but lithological variations may be observed.  Work is ongoing in this respect.

geophysical_update_comment: The Solan sandstone units remain invisible on any seismic dataset due to the lack of Acoustic Impedance contrast between the sands and the enveloping Kimmeridgian shales. Various seismic techniques were modelled in attempts to discriminate between the sands and shales, but all to no avail. The low GOR fluids do not provide any Class III AVO anomalies.The BCU and Base Jurassic are reasonably reliable seismic events, which means that the container may be mapped, but not the fill.
